info.title: nexc-engine API
info.description: Graph engine for LLM-planned, agent-executed task graphs. Errors are RFC 7807 `application/problem+json`. Realtime: SSE `/graphs/{gid}/events` and WebSocket `/graphs/{gid}/ws` authenticated with single-use tickets.

get.summary:
The agent card of an exposed agent, at the well-known address. Public:
an agent that is not exposed is not found.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.description: The exposed agent: its principal (`agent://{workspace}/{name}`) or its id.

get.summary:
The public keys everything nexc signs verifies with, as a JWK set: the
current key and the keys it replaced, each under its `kid` (the RFC 7638
thumbprint of the key). Public, and kept by any cache for five minutes
(`PUBLIC_CACHE_CONTROL`). Run seals, firewall decisions and evidence
bundles name the key they are signed with.

post.summary:
The JSON-RPC endpoint of an exposed agent (A2A): `tasks/send` runs the
task as a one-node run of the agent and answers once it ended or after
25 s with it still working; `tasks/sendSubscribe` streams its status and
artifacts as server-sent events; `tasks/get`, `tasks/cancel` and
`tasks/resubscribe` take the task's id. The caller is a registered
counterpart presenting an agent API token; every task is a `tool_call`
span marked inbound and a `policy` span on the run's trace, and a loop or
a hop past the delegation depth is refused.

parameters.name: principal
parameters.description: The agent's principal, percent-encoded, or its id

200.description: A JSON-RPC response (or an event stream for tasks/sendSubscribe)

401.description: No usable agent API token (a JSON-RPC error)

403.description: The token's agent is not a counterpart, or is out of service

404.description: No exposed agent at that address

get.summary:
The agent card of an exposed agent, under its principal (percent-encoded)
or its id. Public: an agent that is not exposed is not found.

parameters.name: principal
parameters.description: The agent's principal, percent-encoded, or its id

get.summary:
An artifact of a task, for the counterpart that sent it (bearer agent
API token): the file, with `Content-Disposition: attachment`. A file the
DLP classifier kept in is not found until an admin releases it.
What platform administrators did, newest first.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of a name or e-mail address; without control characters.

get.summary: The infrastructure this server runs on (platform administrators).

post.summary:
Checks that a PostgreSQL or Redis server can be reached from this server
with the given URL (server administrators only). Nothing is changed and
the URL is not kept.

get.summary:
The latency of every endpoint this instance served in the last five
minutes, and of the gRPC calls it made (platform administrators).
Each instance answers for itself; behind a load balancer the answer
is one replica's.
Every account of the installation, newest first.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of a name or e-mail address; without control characters.

patch.summary: Changes an account's platform role, suspends it, or lets it back in.
patch.description:
Both a role change and a suspension end the account's access tokens at
once. Nobody changes their own account here, so the platform always
keeps the administrator who is acting. An account that is the only
owner of a workspace other people work in cannot be made a platform
administrator before that workspace has another owner.

409.description: Your own account, or the only owner of a shared workspace

post.summary:
Deletes an account on its holder's request, exactly as the holder could
from their profile: workspaces it is alone in are removed, it leaves the
others, and what identified the person is gone. The activity log keeps
the account's id, not its name or address.

409.description: Your own account, a platform administrator, or the only owner of a shared workspace

422.description: The address does not match

get.summary:
The single sign-on identities linked to an account, with who each is at
its provider (`sub`), oldest first.

delete.summary:
Unlinks a single sign-on identity from an account, and signs the account
out everywhere. The person's next sign-in through the provider is a
first one again: linked by a verified address, or refused. This is what
sorts out an identity the provider re-created (a new `sub`, refused with
`email_taken` until then), one linked by mistake, or one that must not
sign in any more (stop the provider vouching for the address too, or it
is linked again).

204.description: Unlinked; every session of the account ended

post.summary:
Issues a one-time password reset link for an account whose holder cannot
sign in. It works once and for an hour, and replaces any earlier link of
the account that still worked. The administrator hands it over; the
installation sends no e-mail.

get.summary: Every workspace of the installation, newest first.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of a name or e-mail address; without control characters.

get.summary: One workspace: its members and how much it holds, never what it holds.

post.summary:
Deletes a workspace with everything in it, files included. Members it
leaves without any workspace get an empty personal one, so that they can
still sign in and work. The name travels in the body, not in the
address, so that it does not end up in access logs.

422.description: The name does not match

post.summary:
Makes a registered account an owner of a workspace: for a workspace
whose owner left, was suspended or now administers the platform. The
workspace's own audit log records it, so its members see who did it.

409.description: Already an owner, suspended, or a platform administrator

422.description: No account has this address

get.summary: The built-in role templates.

The keys agent tokens verify with: the one the backend signs with first,
then the others it still accepts (`NEXC_AGENT_TOKEN_VERIFY_KEYS`: the
previous key after a rotation, the next one before it). Public: they are
public keys, and the runtime fetches them without credentials; any cache
may keep them for five minutes (`PUBLIC_CACHE_CONTROL`).
The agents of a workspace.

parameters.name: workspace_id
parameters.description: The workspace whose agents to list (default: the caller's first workspace).

post.summary: Adds an agent to a workspace (members and above); audited as `agent_created`.

Makes an agent from a role template (members and above): its
capabilities and purpose from the template, its model allow-list pinned
to the model it is given, its knowledge topics bound where the workspace
has them, the template's policy as the agent's version 1 (audited as
`policy_changed`), and, with a usable provider, its competency questions
asked once and scored on the card. 404 for an unknown template, 409 when
an agent of that name exists.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Template id: analyst, researcher or reviewer

get.summary:
An agent's ID card: who it is, who answers for it, what it may do, what
it has left to spend and what it did last (any member of its workspace).
The card's core is served from the hot-read cache until the agent is
written; its recent spans are read live.

delete.summary:
Removes an agent (its reports no longer report to anyone); audited as
`agent_deleted`.

patch.summary:
Updates an agent (members of its workspace and above). A change of
capabilities raises its policy version and is audited (`policy_changed`).

get.summary:
The tasks an exposed agent received over A2A, newest first (members of
its workspace): who called, the run that answered, the hop and the chain,
and the rule that refused it when the firewall did.

What an agent did last, across runs: its most recent spans, newest
first. Only spans of runs whose graph the caller may open are listed.

post.summary:
Takes an agent out of service (workspace admins): its running nodes are
cancelled, new ones are refused, and its policy version is raised so
that no token minted before is honoured again.
Puts a quarantined agent back in service (workspace admins).

get.summary:
The API tokens of an external agent (workspace admins): prefixes and
dates, never the tokens.

post.summary:
Issues an API token to an external agent (workspace admins). The token
is in the answer once and kept as a hash; audited as `agent_token_issued`.

422.description: The agent is not an external one

delete.summary: Revokes an API token (workspace admins); audited as `agent_token_revoked`.

post.summary: Marks an alert seen (admins of its workspace).

get.summary: One approval (members of its workspace).

post.summary: Lets the call go ahead (an approver named by the policy, or a workspace admin).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1-255 visible ASCII characters: a retry with the same key and body within 24 hours gets the first response again (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`) instead of 409

409.description: Already decided, or a request with this Idempotency-Key is still being handled

422.description: Invalid fields, or an Idempotency-Key used with another request

post.summary:
Refuses the call, with a reason the model sees (an approver named by the
policy, or a workspace admin).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1-255 visible ASCII characters: a retry with the same key and body within 24 hours gets the first response again (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`) instead of 409

409.description: Already decided, or a request with this Idempotency-Key is still being handled

422.description: Invalid fields, or an Idempotency-Key used with another request

get.summary: One file, as of its current version.

delete.summary:
Deletes a file with its versions (everyone but guests who can see it).
Audited as `artifact_file_deleted`.

patch.summary:
Renames a file, moves it to another folder, or attaches it to another
issue or none (everyone but guests who can see it).

409.description: The name is taken in that folder

get.summary: The text of one version of a file (the current one by default).

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version to read (default: the current one).

put.summary:
Saves a new version of a file (everyone but guests who can see it). The
body is the whole new text; `base_version` is the version it was made
from, and someone else's save since then is a 409. Content equal to the
current version's saves nothing and answers the file as it is.

parameters.name: base_version
parameters.description: The version the new content was made from: it must still be the current one.

requestBody.description: The new text (`text/plain` works as well)

409.description: Someone else saved a version first

post.summary:
Copies a file's current version into a new file of the same issue
(everyone but guests who can see it): in the same folder unless another
is given, named with ` copy` (` copy 2`…) unless a name is given.

409.description: The name is taken in that folder

get.summary:
Downloads one version of a file (the current one by default) as an
attachment of plain text; it is never served to be shown, so HTML in it
does not run.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version to read (default: the current one).

get.summary: The versions of a file, newest first.
Downloads one artifact as an attachment.

post.summary:
Releases a quarantined artifact (admins of the run's workspace): it can be
downloaded again. Audited as `artifact_released`.

get.summary: Whether the caller signs in with a second factor.

post.summary:
Turns two-factor sign-in off; asks for the password and a code, so that
a session left open is not enough to do it.

422.description: Wrong password or code

post.summary:
Turns two-factor sign-in on, once the code shows the app was set up. From
then on signing in asks for the app's code after the password.

409.description: Already on, or no setup in progress

422.description: Wrong code

post.summary:
Starts setting up two-factor sign-in: a secret for an authenticator app,
as text and as an `otpauth://` address. Nothing changes about signing in
until `POST /auth/2fa/enable` proves the app has it. An account without a
password (single sign-on created it) has no use for one: it signs in
through the provider, which asks for its own second factor, and could
never turn this one off again (that asks for the password).

409.description: Already on, or the account has no password (it signs in with single sign-on only)

get.summary:
The caller's security activity, newest first: sign-ins and failed
sign-ins with the address they came from, password changes and resets,
reset links created for the account, and what a platform administrator
did to it. Entries are kept for 180 days.

How the caller signs in: whether the account has a password, and the
single sign-on identities linked to it.

post.summary: Verifies credentials and starts a session.

403.description: The account is suspended, or password sign-in is off (single sign-on only) and this is not the break-glass administrator

422.description: The account has two-factor sign-in: `errors.code` asks for the code, or says it is wrong

post.summary: Ends the session: revokes the refresh-token family and clears the cookie.

get.summary: The current user, whichever side of the platform boundary they work on.

patch.summary: Changes the caller's display name.

post.summary:
Deletes the caller's account. Workspaces it is alone in are removed; it
leaves the others, where what it made stays under "Deleted account".
Its name, address, password, sessions, AI account, notifications and
personal memories are gone, and the address can register again.

409.description: The only owner of a shared workspace, or a platform administrator

422.description: Wrong password

get.summary:
A copy of what the installation holds about the caller, as a JSON file:
the account, its workspaces and teams, the issues and comments it wrote,
its graphs, documents and personal memories, and what it spent. No
credential is in it.

Where the provider sends the browser back: the code is exchanged, the ID
token verified, the account found, linked or created, and a session
started as `POST /auth/login` starts one. The browser then goes to the
path it asked for, carrying no token. No second factor is asked: the
provider is the one that authenticates.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The `state` of the authorization request; it works once, for ten minutes.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Set by the provider when the sign-in did not happen there.

parameters.name: error_description
parameters.description: The provider's explanation of `error`; logged, never shown.

parameters.name: iss
parameters.description: The issuer the answer comes from (RFC 9207); when given it must be the configured one.

303.description: Signed in: to the `return_to` path given at the start (the account page after `POST /auth/oidc/link`), with the `nexc_refresh` cookie set (the console then calls `POST /auth/refresh`). Not signed in: to `/login?sso_error=` (`/app/settings/profile?sso_error=` when linking) `unavailable` | `denied` | `expired` | `invalid` | `no_email` | `unverified_email` | `email_taken` | `link_required` | `identity_taken` | `suspended` | `failed`

post.summary:
Links the provider's identity to the signed-in account: the answer names
the provider's authorization URL for the browser to go to (with the
`nexc_sso` cookie set, as `GET /auth/oidc/login` sets it). Whoever signs
in there is linked to this account, whatever address the provider gives,
and the browser comes back to the account page. This is how an account
that is never linked by its address (a platform administrator's, or one
with two-factor sign-in) gets single sign-on. The break-glass account is
never linked: it stays independent of the provider.

200.description: Where to send the browser; the `nexc_sso` cookie is set

409.description: The account is linked to an identity of the provider already, or is the break-glass account

422.description: Wrong password

get.summary: Sends the browser to the provider to sign in.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description:
Where to go once signed in: a path of this site (`/app/...`).
Anything else, an address of another site included, is ignored for `/app`.

303.description: To the provider's authorization endpoint (authorization code with PKCE S256, a `state` and a `nonce` kept here for ten minutes), with the `nexc_sso` cookie binding the sign-in to this browser. When the provider cannot be reached: to `/login?sso_error=unavailable`

post.summary:
Changes the caller's password. Every session ends, on every device, and
this one starts anew: the response carries a fresh access token and
refresh cookie.

422.description: Wrong current password, or a new one that does not meet the rules

post.summary:
Sets a new password with a reset link (no sign-in needed). The link
works once and for an hour. Every session of the account ends; the
person then signs in with the new password. A password that does not
meet the rules does not use the link up.

401.description: The link is unknown, used or expired

422.description: The new password does not meet the rules

get.summary:
The ways to sign in here, for the login page: a password or not,
registration or not, and the single sign-on provider.

post.summary: Rotates the refresh token (cookie + `X-Requested-With: nexc`).

401.description: Missing, expired, revoked or reused refresh token

post.summary: Creates an account (when signups are enabled) and starts a session.

403.description: Signups disabled, or password sign-in is off and accounts come from single sign-on

422.description: Validation failed

get.summary: How many sessions the caller has.

post.summary: Signs the caller out everywhere, this device included.

get.summary: The graphs the caller may work on, most recently updated first.

post.summary: Creates an empty graph in a workspace, or in one of its teams.
Creates a new graph from a template.

get.summary: A graph with nodes and edges. Supports `If-None-Match` (304).

delete.summary:
Deletes a graph. It is archived, not erased: it disappears from every list
and can no longer be opened, run or changed; its queued runs are cancelled
and its running ones asked to stop; and its runs, with their hash-chained
spans, signed seals, payload metadata and artifacts, stay readable as
evidence (`GET /runs/{rid}/trace/verify`, `GET /runs/{rid}/evidence`)
until the retention purge removes the graph for good. The deletion is a
`graph_deleted` entry in the workspace's audit log.

patch.summary: Updates name, description or goal.

get.summary: Topological order, parallel levels, critical path, cycles and components.

post.summary: Adds an edge; an edge of a blocking relation that would create a cycle is a 409.

409.description: Would create a cycle, or already exists

delete.summary: Deletes an edge.

patch.summary: Rewrites why an edge exists.

get.summary: Server-sent events of a graph (contract §6).

post.summary: Adds a node.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1-255 visible ASCII characters: a retry with the same key and body within 24 hours gets the first response again (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`) instead of a second node

409.description: A request with this Idempotency-Key is still being handled (`Retry-After`)

422.description: Invalid fields, or an Idempotency-Key used with another request

delete.summary: Deletes a node and its edges.

patch.summary: Updates a node.

put.summary:
Replaces the graph's vocabulary (its node types and relation types) in
onto-intelli, as the caller: nexc checks its own rules, then plans and
applies the change there in one audited write and tells the graph's
sockets (`ontology.updated`). Read-only while onto-intelli is off.

403.description: onto-intelli refused the caller (a guest is a viewer there)

409.description: A relation made blocking would create a cycle, or onto-intelli is off (read-only)

422.description: Invalid, a type still in use was removed, or onto-intelli refused a field

post.summary: Starts planning; progress streams over SSE (`plan.*` events).

422.description: No LLM API key configured

get.summary: A plan of a graph.

post.summary: Applies a ready plan to the graph.

get.summary:
Runs of a graph, newest first (at most 100). A deleted graph's runs are
listed too, for those who could open it: their evidence is kept until the
retention purge (`GET /runs/{rid}/evidence`).

post.summary: Queues a run; progress streams over SSE (`run.*`, `node.*` events).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1-255 visible ASCII characters: a retry with the same key and body within 24 hours gets the first response again (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`) instead of a second run

409.description: A request with this Idempotency-Key is still being handled (`Retry-After`)

422.description: Invalid selection, no LLM API key configured, or an Idempotency-Key used with another request

get.summary: Dependency suggestions (similarity + BM25, near-duplicates skipped).

Collaborative WebSocket of a graph (contract §7). The `Origin` header,
when present, must be one of `NEXC_CORS_ORIGINS`.
Liveness: the process serves HTTP.
One issue.

delete.summary: Deletes an issue (a graph created for it stays).

patch.summary:
Updates an issue. Moving it to a completed or canceled state stamps
`completed_at`; moving it back clears it.

post.summary: Comments on an issue. Whoever may edit the issue may comment on it.
post.description:
Each member the comment mentions who can see the issue hears of it in
their inbox (`mention`), in place of the `comment` entry the assignee and
the creator get. The first active agent it mentions is delegated an issue
that has none; then, when the author is a member of the issue's team and
the issue's graph is idle, one mentioned agent is asked for a plan (the
issue gets its graph if it has none). The plan waits to be applied like
any other: nothing runs by itself. Both show in the timeline as `agent`
entries.

delete.summary: Deletes a comment: its author, or whoever manages the team.

patch.summary: Edits a comment. Only its author can.
patch.description:
Only the mentions the edit adds act: the members it newly mentions are
told, and agents it newly mentions are handed the issue as on a new
comment. Nobody hears of the same mention twice.

get.summary:
The timeline of an issue, oldest first: its comments, the changes to its
state, priority, assignee, title, due date and GitHub link, what happened
to its files, and what its runs reported.

post.summary:
Gives the issue a graph that plans and executes it: a graph of the issue's
team whose goal is the issue's title and description. Calling it again
returns the issue with the graph it already has.

403.description: Only team members run its issues

get.summary:
The files the runs of the issue's graph produced, newest run first, with
the run each came from; empty when the issue has no graph or the caller
cannot read its runs. They download from `/artifacts/{aid}/download`.

post.summary:
Keeps a file a run of the issue's graph produced among the issue's files
(everyone but guests who can see the issue and its runs), named after
the file (with ` copy` when the name is taken). Only a text file of at
most 1 MiB can be kept, and not while it is quarantined.

get.summary:
Lists (newest first) or searches the memory of a workspace: what its
graphs learned, as far as the caller can open those graphs, plus the
caller's own notes.

parameters.name: workspace_id
parameters.description: The workspace whose memory to read (default: the caller's first workspace).

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Restrict to a graph (plus the caller's user-scope memories).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Hybrid search query; results then carry a `score`. Without control characters.

parameters.name: topic_id
parameters.description: Only memories grouped under this topic.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many results to skip, for paging (0–5000, default 0).

parameters.name: preview
parameters.description:
Cut each `content` to this many characters (20–2000) and end it with `…`: a list
shows previews and reads the whole memory with `GET /memories/{id}` when it is opened.

get.summary:
The topics of a workspace's memory, largest first, with how many memories
of each the caller may read. They are found without supervision: memories
are clustered by their embeddings and each cluster is named by the words
that set it apart, drawn only from memories the whole workspace can read.

post.summary:
Finds the topics of a workspace's memory afresh (admins and owners). The
work runs in the background; read the topics again shortly.

get.summary:
One memory in full, if the caller may read it: their own notes, and what
the graphs they can open learned.

delete.summary:
Forgets a memory. Its author may, and so may anyone who can work on the
graph it was learned in.

patch.summary: Classifies a memory (admins of its workspace). Audited as `classification_changed`.

get.summary: Queue, running work, agents and backend health for the caller.
Readiness: the instance is not shutting down and the database answers.

503.description: Draining (shutting down, its runs handed to the other replicas) or database unavailable

post.summary: Issues a single-use ticket for one of the caller's graphs.

get.summary: One run with its node results.

post.summary:
Stops one sub-agent of a running run, named by the `spawn` span it was
born in; the run goes on. The runtime cancels the sub-agent's task and its
parent sees the tool error "cancelled by an operator"; the stop is a
`policy` span of decision `cancelled` on the trace and an
`agent_cancelled` entry in the audit log (whoever may cancel the run).

202.description: The stop is recorded and on its way

get.summary: Artifacts of a run.
All artifacts of a run as a zip (`<node_id>/<path>` entries).

post.summary: Cancels a queued or running run.

get.summary:
A run's evidence bundle: every span in chain order, the signed seal, the
payloads' metadata (never their content), the workspace's audit entries
about the run and its graph as chained, and the backend's signed
attestation over all of it. `nexc-verify` (or `make verify-bundle`)
checks it with the keys of `/.well-known/jwks.json` alone. For workspace
owners and admins (the readers of the audit log), deleted graphs' runs
included; the export is itself an `evidence_exported` entry, carried by
the bundle.

The run as a tree: its nodes, the agent each ran as, the sub-agents it
spawned, with status, times, tokens, cost, calls and denials per subtree
and the ids to open its spans (whoever may open the run).
The spans of a run in id order (UUID v7: the order they started), paged.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Return spans whose id is greater than this one (the `next` of the previous page).

get.summary:
Recomputes the run's hash chain from the stored spans and compares it
with what is stored and with the hash sealed when the run finished, and
checks the seal's signature with the key published under its `kid`. A
deleted graph's runs verify as before.

The LLM settings that apply to the caller: their own account, else the
credential of the workspace they name, else the server defaults.

parameters.name: workspace_id
parameters.description:
The workspace the caller is working in; its credential applies when
they have not connected an account of their own.

put.summary:
Connects the caller's own account: provider, model, base URL and
(encrypted) API key. It takes precedence over any workspace credential.

delete.summary:
Disconnects the caller's own account, so the workspace's credential (or
the server default) applies to their work again.

get.summary:
The models the provider behind the caller's effective settings offers
right now, newest first. Asked from the provider, never from a built-in list.

parameters.name: workspace_id
parameters.description:
The workspace the caller is working in; its credential applies when
they have not connected an account of their own.

422.description: The provider could not be asked

get.summary:
The recorded payloads of a span (the run's owner and the workspace's
admins; other members 403; outsiders 404). Reading is audited as
`payload_viewed` when there was something to read; a span recorded
nothing answers with no payloads.
The built-in templates.
The workspaces the caller belongs to.

post.summary: Creates a workspace; the caller becomes its owner.

get.summary: One workspace the caller belongs to.

delete.summary:
Deletes a workspace with everything in it (owners only). A user's last
workspace cannot be deleted: every account works in at least one.

patch.summary: Renames a workspace (admins and owners).

get.summary: The A2A counterparts of a workspace (members and above).

post.summary:
Registers a remote A2A agent (admins): its card is fetched and validated
at once (a card that does not answer is still registered, with the
failure on it), an external agent principal `a2a:<name>` is made for its
inbound calls, and the first API token of that principal is in the answer
once. Audited as `a2a_counterpart_added`.

get.summary: One counterpart of the workspace.

delete.summary:
Removes a counterpart with its principal (admins): its tool stops being
offered at the next run and its tokens stop working at once. Audited as
`a2a_counterpart_removed`.

post.summary: Fetches the counterpart's card again and records what it says (admins).

get.summary: The alert destinations of a workspace (admins).

post.summary:
Registers a destination (admins). The signing secret is in the answer
once and never shown again; the URL is kept encrypted.

get.summary: One destination (admins).

delete.summary: Removes a destination and its delivery log (admins).

patch.summary:
Changes a destination (admins): name, URL, filters, on or off. Enabling
one the platform switched off clears its failure count.

get.summary: The delivery log of a destination, newest first (admins).

post.summary:
Sends a test event to the destination at once and says what it answered

PlatformMember.description: A member of a workspace, as the platform sees them.

suspended.description:
Whether the account can use the workspace at all: a suspended account
and a platform administrator cannot.

PlatformUser.description: An account as the platform sees it.

locked.description: Whether sign-in is locked right now (too many failed attempts).

role.description: `admin` administers the platform; `user` is everyone else.

suspended.description: Whether a platform administrator suspended the account, and why.

two_factor.description: Whether the account signs in with a second factor.

workspace_count.description: Workspaces the account belongs to, and how many of them it owns.

PlatformWorkspace.description: A workspace as the platform sees it: who owns it and how big it is.

owner_name.description: Its first owner, by name and e-mail; `null` when it has none.

PlatformWorkspaceDetail.description: One workspace with its members and its size.

Policy.description: One stored version of a policy.

scope_id.description: The team or agent; `null` at the workspace level.

PolicyDocument.description: One version of a policy. `{}` sets nothing and inherits everything.

labels.description: The classifications agents under this policy may read; `null` inherits.

time_windows.description: When agents may start work; `null` inherits, `[]` never.

PolicyInForce.description: A policy version in force at one level.

PolicyScope.description: The level a policy is set at.

PolicyVersions.description:
The versions of the policies that governed a node, by level; `null`
where no policy is set.

Project.description:
A project: a body of work that issues of any team can belong to, owned
by one team or by the workspace as a whole.

closed_count.description: Of those, the ones in a completed or canceled state.

issue_count.description: Issues of the project the caller can see.

oneOf.description: That team's key and name, for display.

team_id.description: The team that owns the project; `null` for a project of the whole workspace.

ProposalStatus.description: Where a schema change proposal stands in onto-intelli.

ProposedEdge.description: A typed relation between two proposed nodes (by `ref`).

kind.description: Key of a relation type; empty means the ontology's dependency relation.

reason.description: Why the two nodes are related this way.

ProposedNode.description: A node in a plan proposal. `ref` is a plan-local identifier used by edges.

existing_id.description:
Id of the existing node this refines, or `null` for a new node.
Malformed ids from the model are read as `null`.

kind.description: Key of a node type: one of the graph's, or one the plan's ontology adds.

Recording.description:
What is kept of what agents say and hear, off by default: the prompt and
the completion of every model turn, the input and output of every tool
call, each for `retention_days`, with the passages and memories of the
labels in `redact_labels` replaced by their citation before anything is
written (`domain::recording`).

redact_labels.description: Labels whose passages and memories are replaced by their citation id in every payload.

retention_days.description: Days a payload is kept (1–3650; default 30); a worker deletes older ones.

recovery_codes.description: Each signs in once in place of the app's code. Only digests are kept.

RegisteredA2aCounterpart.description: A counterpart just registered, with the token its inbound calls present.

token.description: The API token issued to the counterpart's principal: `nexc_agt_…`, shown once.

RelationType.description: A type of relation between two nodes.

blocking.description:
The source must finish before the target runs. Blocking relations form
the execution DAG and may not close a cycle.

description.description: What the relation asserts about source and target.

token.description: The token of a reset link, as a platform administrator issued it.

Resolved.description: The effective policy of an agent and where each rule came from.

capabilities.description: What the per-run token carries: the agent's capabilities narrowed by every level.

levels.description: The policy versions in force, outermost first.

origins.description:
Rule path (`tools.allow`, `limits.tokens_per_run`, ...) → the level that set it
(`workspace`, `team`, `agent`, `capabilities` for the agent's own document, `default`).

RiskPoint.description: The highest risk score an agent was given on one day.

RiskyAgent.description: One of the agents whose latest run strayed furthest from its baseline.

Rollup.description: What a subtree spent and did.

tokens_cached.description: Of `tokens_in`, the ones read from the provider's prompt cache.

RpcRequest.description: A JSON-RPC request as the endpoint reads it.

RpcResponse.description: A JSON-RPC response: `result` on success, `error` otherwise.

RuleAction.description: What a finding leads to: a word in the inbox, or a refusal.

Rules.description:
Everything the resolved policy says beyond the capabilities: carried in
the per-run token next to them and evaluated by the same functions on
both sides. `Rules::default()` is what an agent gets when no policy is set.

time_windows.description: One set of windows per level that set some; a time must be in a window of every set.

tools_denied.description: Tools refused whatever the allow-list says.

Run.description: One execution of (part of) a graph.

policy_mismatches.description:
Actions the runtime reported that the policy minted for the run did
not allow (each one is a `policy_mismatch` audit entry and a `policy` span).

policy_versions.description: The workspace policy version that governed the run (each node run has every level).

seal_kid.description:
The key the seal is signed with (`/.well-known/jwks.json`); `null` while the run
runs, when nothing was traced, and for runs sealed before seals were signed.

trace_hash.description:
Hex SHA-256 sealing the run's trace chain once it finished; `null`
while it runs or when nothing was traced (`GET /runs/{id}/trace/verify`).

RunArtifact.description: A file a run of an issue's graph produced, with the run it came from.

RunCounts.description: Runs in a window, by outcome.

SchemaProposal.description: A schema change proposal, as nexc lists it; people review it in onto-intelli.

breaking.description: Whether applying it would break data or vocabulary in use.

proposer.description: Who filed it: `user:{id}`, or `assistant:{user id}` for the assistant.

review_url.description: Where to review it in onto-intelli's UI; `null` when its address is unknown.

SealVerification.description: Whether a run's signed seal holds.

kid.description: The key the seal is signed with (`/.well-known/jwks.json`).

ok.description:
True when the signature verifies with the published key named by
`kid` and the signed statement names this run and this chain.

reason.description: Why it does not hold, when `ok` is false.

sealed_at.description: When the run was sealed, as signed.

SearchHit.description: One thing that matched a search.

subtitle.description: What tells it apart: an issue's state, a team's key, an e-mail.

title.description: An issue's identifier and title, a project's or graph's name, a person's name.

SecopsOverview.description:
Everything the top of the console shows, in one call. Runs, spans and
denials count only what the caller may open.

alerts_open.description: Unacknowledged alerts by severity (severities with none are left out).

artifacts_quarantined.description: Artifacts the DLP screen kept in and nobody released.

denials_fortnight.description: Policy denials over the last fourteen days, by rule.

denials_today.description: Policy denials since midnight UTC, by the rule that denied.

evidence_today.description: Outputs that answered since midnight UTC, by evidence verdict.

policy_versions.description: The latest version at every level that has one.

risk_history.description: The highest score per agent per day over the last fourteen days, oldest first.

runs_week.description: Runs created in the last seven days.

top_risk.description: The five agents scoring highest, highest first; only agents scored at least once.

SecopsSpan.description:
A span as the trace explorer lists it: the identifiers and the few
attributes the table shows, never the whole attribute document.

decision.description: `attributes.decision` of a policy or approval span.

evidence.description:
`attributes.evidence`: the verdict on an output, on the node's `evidence`
policy span (and on the built-in executor's one model call).

host.description: `attributes.egress_host`: the host a tool called out to.

inbound.description: `attributes.inbound`: a tool call that is a task received over A2A.

tool.description: `attributes.tool` of a tool call or a policy decision about one.

SecopsSpanPage.description: A page of the trace explorer, newest first.

next.description: Pass as `before` for the next page; `null` on the last.

by_model.description: Usage by model, most costly first.

recording.description: Whether prompts and completions were being recorded when the run's nodes started.

SessionAgent.description:
One agent of a node: the agent the node ran as (depth 0) or a sub-agent
it spawned, with its own turns and tool calls and what hangs under it.

cancellable.description: Whether an operator may stop it now: a sub-agent still working in a node still running.

children.description: The sub-agents it spawned, in birth order.

depth.description: 0 for the agent the node ran as.

own.description: The agent's own turns and tool calls.

principal.description: `agent://{workspace}/{name}`, sub-agents `…/{role}-{n}`; `system` for a node without an agent.

role.description: The role a sub-agent was spawned as.

span_ids.description: Its own spans in chain order: turns, tool calls, policy decisions, approvals.

spawn_span_id.description: The `spawn` span a sub-agent was born in (what `POST /runs/{id}/agents/{span_id}/cancel` names); `null` at depth 0.

total.description: Its own plus every sub-agent under it.

SessionAgentRef.description: An agent that worked in a run, as the list names it.

agents.description: The agent the node ran as, with its sub-agents under it.

cached.description: Served from the result cache: no agent worked.

context_span_ids.description: What the node was given before it ran (`data_read`) and what was withheld (`policy` named `context`).

SessionPage.description: A page of a workspace's sessions, newest first.

next.description: Pass as `before` for the next page; `null` on the last.

SessionStatus.description: Where a node or an agent subtree stands.

SessionSummary.description: One row of a workspace's session list: a run with its rollups.

agents.description: The workspace agents that ran its nodes.

active.description: Sign-ins that are still alive, this one included.

classification.description: The classification of every passage under the topic, on top of its document's.

label.description: The classification agents need clearance for to recall the memory.

oneOf.description: Defaults to `member`.

Setup.description: What an authenticator app is set up with.

secret.description: The secret, to type into the app when it cannot open the address.

uri.description: The `otpauth://` address the app adds the account from.

identities.description: The provider identities linked to the account, oldest first.

password.description: Whether the account has a password; one single sign-on created has none.

Span.description:
One span of a run's trace, as stored and as served (and as an evidence
bundle carries it, to be read back by the offline verifier).

attributes.description: Digests, sizes, counts and ids. Never tool arguments, never secrets.

hash.description: Hex SHA-256 of `prev_hash` and this span's canonical JSON.

name.description: The tool, the model, or what was read.

parent_id.description: The turn a tool call belongs to; the spawn a sub-agent's turns belong to.

prev_hash.description: Hex SHA-256 of the previous span in the chain (zeros for the first).

principal.description: Who acted: the agent's name as the runtime reports it, `system` for the backend.

seq.description: Position in the run's chain (order of receipt).

SpanKind.description: What kind of action a span records.

SpanPayload.description: One recorded payload of a span, decrypted.

redactions.description: Passages and memories replaced by their citation, plus credentials scrubbed.

size.description: Bytes of the content as kept.

SpanPayloads.description:
What `GET /spans/{id}/payload` answers: the span's payloads with the
classifications of the data its node was given, for the banner.

labels.description: The classifications of the data the node was given: what the content may be derived from.

payloads.description: Whether anything was recorded for the span; empty when recording was off.

oneOf.description: One span appended to a run's trace chain (contract §6).
Something about an agent needs a look (contract §6).

SseEvent.description: One server-sent event (`data:` payload). The variant determines the SSE `event:` name.

SsoProvider.description: A single sign-on provider the login page offers.

display_name.description: What the button says after "Continue with".

login_url.description:
Where the button sends the browser (`GET`, a navigation), with
`?return_to=<path of this site>`.

redis_url.description:
`redis://[:password@]host:6379` the workspace moves to, if any. The
server keeps nothing durable in Redis; it is checked and told of the
handover. Neither stored nor logged.

url.description:
`postgres://user:password@host:5432/database` of the database that
should receive the workspace. Used for this transfer only: it is
neither stored nor logged. The user needs the right to create tables.

StateCategory.description:
What a workflow state means, whatever a team calls it. Reports and
"is this done?" questions use the category, never the name.

SubIssueCount.description: How many sub-issues an issue has, and how many of them are closed.

TableReport.description: What a transfer copied for one table.

read.description: Rows of the workspace on this server.

written.description: Rows written to the target (fewer when a row was already there).

Team.description: A team as seen by the caller.

key.description: Short identifier that prefixes the team's issues, e.g. `ENG`.

oneOf.description: The caller's role in the team, if they are a member.

TeamRef.description: A team, as much as a project shows of the team that owns it.

TeamRole.description: Role of a user in a team.

TimeWindow.description: When the agent may start work (UTC). `days` are ISO weekdays, 1 = Monday.

end.description: `HH:MM`; a window ending before it starts wraps past midnight.

TimelineDay.description: How much happened on one day.

TimelineEntry.description: One thing that happened in a workspace.

actor.description: Who did it, by name; `null` for what the system did or whose account is gone.

entity_id.description: The id of that thing, when it can be opened.

kind.description:
What happened: an audit action (`member_added`, `team_created`, …),
`issue_created`, `issue_state`, `issue_comment`, `issue_assignee`,
`issue_priority`, `issue_title`, `graph_created`, `run_succeeded`,
`run_failed` (and the other run statuses), `document_added`,
`memories_learned`.

title.description: Its name as it was shown: an issue's identifier and title, a graph's name.

Topic.description: A topic of a workspace's documents, found by clustering their passages.

classification.description: Classification of every passage under the topic, on top of its document's.

label.description: The words that set the topic apart: "customs · invoices · port".

TracePage.description: A page of a run's trace.

next.description: Pass as `after` to get the next page; `null` on the last page.

spans.description: Spans in id order (UUID v7: the order they started).

TraceSeal.description: The run whose trace chain was sealed last.

trace_hash.description: Hex SHA-256 of the chain's last span.

TraceVerification.description: Result of recomputing a run's chain.

oneOf.description: The first span that does not fit, when `ok` is false.

hash.description: Hex hash of the last span, `null` for an empty chain.

ok.description:
True when every span hashes as stored, every link holds, and the
sealed hash (if the run is finished) is the chain's last hash.

oneOf.description:
The check of the run's signed seal; `null` while it runs, when nothing
was traced, and for runs sealed before seals were signed.

sealed_hash.description: Hex hash written when the run finished, `null` while it runs or if nothing was traced.

Transfer.description: A transfer of a workspace and how it went.

redis_target.description: The Redis it moved to, without credentials; empty when none was named.

report.description: Per table: rows read here and rows written there.

target.description: Where the data went, without credentials.

TransferCheck.description: What a connection check found, for each target the owner named.

database.description: The database's version, or why it could not be reached.

TurnOutcome.description: What an assistant turn did besides answering, kept with its message.

TwoFactor.description: Whether an account signs in with a second factor.

recovery_codes_left.description: Recovery codes that were not used yet.

TwoFactorCode.description: A code from the authenticator app.

UpdateAgent.description: `PATCH /agents/{id}` body (any subset; `reports_to: null` and `team_id: null` detach).

a2a_exposed.description:
Publishes the agent as an A2A agent, or withdraws it (workspace admins;
audited as `agent_a2a_changed`; not for an `external` agent).

oneOf.description: Replaces the whole document; raises the policy version when it differs.
`active` or `paused`; quarantine has its own routes.

folder_id.description: The folder to move it into; `null` moves it to the top level.

issue_id.description: An issue of the workspace to attach it to; `null` detaches it.

name.description: A new name; its extension must be a text file's.

parent_id.description: The folder to move it into; `null` moves it to the top level.

UpdateIssue.description:
`PATCH /issues/{iid}` body: any subset. `assignee_id`, `agent_id`,
`project_id`, `due_date` and `github_url` accept `null` to clear them.

cycle_id.description: A cycle of the issue's team; `null` takes the issue out of its cycle.

due_date.description: The day the issue is due (`YYYY-MM-DD`); `null` removes it.

github_url.description:
A GitHub issue or pull request the issue is about; `null` or blank removes the link.
A trailing slash, a fragment or a query is dropped, and `http://` or `www.` becomes
`https://github.com/`.

parent_id.description: The issue this one is part of; `null` makes it an issue of its own.

api_key.description: Leave out to keep the stored key, send `""` to remove it.

embed_base_url.description:
An OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`https://api.openai.com/v1`); `null` or
empty uses the server's, else the built-in embedding.

embed_dims.description: Vector size to ask for, when the model can shorten its vectors (64-4096).

UpdateLlmSettings.description:
`PUT /settings/llm` body. `api_key`: omitted keeps the stored key,
`""` deletes it, any other value replaces it.

UpdateNode.description:
`PATCH /graphs/{gid}/nodes/{nid}` body: any subset of the mutable node
fields. `agent_role` and `output` accept `null` to clear them.

kind.description: Key of a node type of the graph's ontology.

UpdatePlatformUser.description: `PATCH /admin/users/{uid}` body: at least one of `role` and `suspended`.

reason.description: Why the account is suspended (with `suspended: true`), for the activity log.

oneOf.description: `admin` lets the account administer the platform; `user` takes that away.

suspended.description: `true` stops the account from signing in and ends its sessions; `false` lifts that.

two_factor.description:
`false` turns the account's two-factor sign-in off, for someone who
lost their authenticator app and their recovery codes.

team_id.description: The team that owns the project; `null` gives it to the whole workspace.

UsageReport.description: Token usage of a workspace over the last `days` days.

by_credential.description: Whose account paid: members' own, the workspace's, or the server's.

by_day.description: Oldest first; days without usage are absent.

by_member.description: Highest cost first, then most tokens.

scope.description: `workspace` for admins; other members get a report of their own usage.

UsageScope.description: Whether a report covers the whole workspace or only the caller.

key.description: Whose LLM configuration is in effect.

UsageSlice_ConfigScope.description: Usage of one group (a day, a member, a model, ...).

UsageSlice_String.description: Usage of one group (a day, a member, a model, ...).

key.description: A member a slice of usage belongs to.

user_id.description: `null` for a member whose account was deleted.

UsageSlice_UsageMember.description: Usage of one group (a day, a member, a model, ...).

key.description: A provider and model a slice of usage ran on.

UsageSlice_UsageModel.description: Usage of one group (a day, a member, a model, ...).

key.description: What an LLM call was for.

UsageSlice_UsagePurpose.description: Usage of one group (a day, a member, a model, ...).

UsageTotals.description: Sums over a set of calls.

context_chars_saved.description:
Characters of upstream context that were not sent because they were
padding or irrelevant to the task. Roughly four characters make a token.

Workspace.description: A workspace as seen by one of its members.

WorkspaceFootprint.description: How much a workspace holds, in counts.

WorkspaceInvite.description: An invitation that waits for its recipient to sign up.

suspended.description:
Suspended by a platform administrator: the account cannot sign in
until that is lifted, which is not the workspace's to decide.

WorkspaceRole.description: Role of a user in a workspace, from most to least privileged.
